terraform-architecture-assertion-review..text:
Found one concrete regression:

- **Both architectures can incorrectly resolve to stateful.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:100](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:100), canonical branch recognition accepts `under service` but misses `in the service branch` and `within the service branch`. Executing the current detector confirmed that `"workload port in the service branch or stateful_service branch"` returns `"stateful"`; the equivalent `under` query remains unresolved. Consequently, the shared consumer gate removes canonical `service` candidates despite explicit alternatives.

Recognize these canonical branch references as positive stateless evidence so both assertions preserve choices. The added tests cover only the `under` variant.

Review remained read-only and source-only; no benchmark qualification.

terraform-architecture-clause-review.txt.text:
Source-only review found four concrete detector bugs:

- **P1 — Punctuation bypasses the negative guard.** `workload port, not necessarily stateful, please` resolves to `stateful_service.port` as a leaf. The lookahead excludes commas and question marks. [Line 78](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:78)
- **P1 — The six-word bound silently converts negative paths into positive intent.** `workload port, not in the selected public listener configuration for stateful_service.public` selects `stateful_service.port`. This should remain unresolved. [Line 78](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:78)
- **P2 — Case-insensitive matching uses case-sensitive captures.** `without stateful` remains unresolved, but `WITHOUT stateful` resolves to stateful. [Line 83](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:83)
- **P2 — Unrelated constraints suppress explicit architecture.** `stateless workload port without host rewriting for the service` returns both architecture choices: the parser mistakes generic “service” for an architecture reference. [Lines 78–87](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:78)

Verified with read-only Bun calls against the current detector and selection consumer. The architecture gate remains workload-scoped, and the SQL change preserves provider/node filters. Existing regression assertions miss these cases.

No edits, other agents, GitHub actions, or benchmark qualification performed.

terraform-architecture-finalreview.txt.text:
Found three concrete issues; source-only approval should remain withheld.

1. **Negative stateful paths still resolve architecture.** In [terraform-property-ranking.ts:90](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:90), `workload port, not under stateful_service.public` resolves **stateful**, while `not stateful_service.public` resolves **stateless**. Both should remain unresolved under the stated negative-path policy. `without stateful` also incorrectly resolves stateful.

2. **Unresolved intent can become a decided branch downstream.** Although the architecture helper returns undefined for `not necessarily stateful`, [terraform-branch-choices.ts:47](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-branch-choices.ts:47) still treats `stateful` as positive branch evidence and narrows to `stateful_service`. Similarly, [terraform-property-selection.ts:244](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-selection.ts:244) skips the architecture collision guard for uncertain architecture words or negative `service.public` mentions; later token matching can accept the mentioned branch. The new ranking assertions do not verify these downstream cases.

3. **Parenthetical `e.g.` examples are not stripped reliably.** The regex at [terraform-property-ranking.ts:76](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:76) requires `\b` after the final period. There is no word boundary between that period and the usual following space, so `workload port (e.g. stateful_service.public)` incorrectly hard-filters to stateful. The same pattern affects identifier extraction.

The SQL workload exception remains inside an AND clause, preserving provider/node filters. Per-candidate identifier handling addresses the mixed-provider ordering issue, and the added conflict guard is workload-scoped.

No edits, agents, authentication, tests, or benchmarks performed. The reported 281 passes and pinned-resolver result were not independently verified.

terraform-architecture-guard-review.txt.text:
Two concrete failures remain:

- **P1 — Negative bare branch mentions select the excluded architecture.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:79](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:79), the negative-path guard requires `.` or `/`. Actual detector probes show `workload port, not under service` resolves **stateless**, and `not under stateful_service` resolves **stateful**. Backticked `service` also fails. The shared consumer filter then removes the opposite architecture instead of preserving choices.

- **P2 — Unrelated negative context suppresses explicit architecture.** The global guards at [lines 77–78](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:77) return unresolved for `stateless workload port without host rewriting` and `stateful workload port, not necessarily public`. Both retain both architectures despite explicit intent. These guards need architecture-related scope.

The added regressions cover dotted negative paths, but miss these cases. Other-provider architecture filtering remains bypassed by the provider guard.

Read-only source review and direct detector probes only; no edits, benchmark qualification, or independent confirmation of the reported 285 passes.

terraform-architecture-lastreview.txt.text:
Two concrete failures remain in the detector:

- **Negative paths with articles after the preposition select an architecture.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:85](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:85), `not under a service.public path` returns `stateless`; `not under the stateful_service.public path` returns `stateful`. The guard accepts articles before `under`, but not after it. Both should remain unresolved.

- **Uncertain canonical paths select stateless.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:78](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:78), both `not necessarily service.public` and `not necessarily under service.public` return `stateless`. The uncertainty guard covers architecture adjectives and `stateful_service`, but omits canonical service paths.

Both results propagate through the shared architecture gate, removing the opposite workload branch before ranking or selection.

Confirmed these outputs by evaluating the current detector in memory. Explicit `service.public or stateful_service.public` correctly remains unresolved; the architecture gate remains workload-only. No edits, agents, GitHub actions, authentication, or benchmark qualification performed.

terraform-architecture-negative-review.t.text:
Found three concrete detector bugs; I would hold source approval.

- **Backtick-qualified negation selects the opposite of the requested architecture.** For `workload port, not `stateful``, the negative parser accepts direct negation, but the final inversion regex cannot cross the backtick. It returns `stateful`, excluding canonical `service`. Negated backticked `stateless` similarly returns `stateless`. [Lines 87–98](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:87)

- **Unrelated negative clauses swallow later explicit architecture.** `workload port without host rewriting, stateful` returns unresolved: the negative regex spans the comma and treats `stateful` as governed by `without`. Consumers consequently retain both architectures despite explicit stateful intent. [Lines 77–92](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:77)

- **Article-qualified canonical branches can incorrectly resolve alternatives.** `workload port under the service branch or stateful_service branch` returns `stateful`: positive canonical detection requires `under service`, missing `under the service`. The shared gate then removes canonical `service` instead of preserving both choices. [Lines 94–106](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:94)

The added tests do not cover these cases. The architecture gate remains workload-scoped, and I found no concrete change to other-provider filtering in the reviewed consumers.

Read-only source review only; no edits, agents, GitHub actions, or benchmark qualification. I did not independently rerun the reported 288 passing tests.

terraform-architecture-rereview.txt.text:
Found three concrete source issues in the latest diff:

- **P1 — Negative context can select the wrong architecture.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:82](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:82) only recognizes adjacent `not stateful` / `not stateless`. `"workload port, not a stateful service"` selects stateful and removes canonical `service`. `"workload port, not necessarily stateful"` also incorrectly resolves architecture.

- **P1 — Explicit service-path detection includes excluded references.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:79](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:79) interprets `"workload port, not under service.public"` as stateless and removes `stateful_service`. Likewise, `"workload port (for example service.public)"` hard-selects stateless even though existing query processing excludes such examples.

- **P2 — Identifier suppression depends on scope or candidate order.** [terraform-property-index.ts:210](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-index.ts:210) retains the hard `stateful_service` SQL filter when `providerName` is absent. Thus an unscoped `"stateless or stateful_service workload port"` loses canonical candidates before ranking. [terraform-property-selection.ts:61](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-selection.ts:61) similarly applies one identifier policy to all rows based on the first row’s provider, making mixed-provider filtering order-dependent.

The added tests cover simple negation, both architecture terms, and a homogeneous other-provider service-path case; they miss these cases. Provider/node SQL predicates remain intact.

Source-only review completed. No edits, agents, GitHub changes, authentication, test execution, or benchmark qualification; the reported 278 passes were not independently verified.

terraform-architecture-shared-review.txt.text:
Three concrete issues remain in the shared architecture detector:

- **P1 — Explicit alternatives can discard canonical service.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:84](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:84): `workload port under service.public or stateful_service.public` resolves to **stateful**. Canonical `service` contributes architecture intent only when neither adjective is detected. The shared gate consequently removes canonical candidates, and identifier extraction retains the hard `stateful_service` constraint. Both explicit architectures should remain unresolved.

- **P2 — Articles bypass uncertainty handling.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:77](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:77): `workload port, not necessarily a stateful service` resolves to **stateful**, because the uncertainty guard requires the architecture immediately after `necessarily`. Likewise, `workload port without a stateful service` bypasses the `without` guard. Both incorrectly remove canonical service choices.

- **P2 — Article-qualified negative paths become architecture decisions.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:81](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:81): `workload port, not a stateful_service.public` bypasses the negative-path guard, then matches the article-qualified reversal at line 96 and resolves to **stateless**. This contradicts the intended unresolved handling of negative path mentions.

The added tests do not cover these variants. I found no concrete regression in other-provider architecture behavior or the retained provider/node SQL filters.

Source review only; no edits, agents, GitHub changes, test execution, or benchmark qualification.

terraform-architecture-syntax-review.txt.text:
One concrete bug remains in [terraform-property-ranking.ts](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:98): conflicting positive and negative assertions of the same architecture resolve instead of remaining undecided.

Verified against the current detector:

- `stateful workload port; not stateful` → `stateless`
- `stateless workload port; not stateless` → `stateful`

The detector collapses occurrences into token-presence booleans, then reverses intent if any direct negation exists. Its consumers consequently exclude one workload architecture despite conflicting intent. The added tests don’t cover this case.

No additional concrete regression found in the reviewed diff’s provider scoping or identifier handling. Read-only source review only; no benchmark qualification or independent confirmation of the reported 289 passes.

terraform-architecture-ubuntu-review.txt.text:
Source review found three concrete bugs:

- **P1 — Negated architecture selects the excluded branch.** [terraform-property-ranking.ts:77](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:77) treats keyword presence as positive intent. `workload port, not stateful` removes canonical `service` and retains `stateful_service`; `not stateless` does the reverse. The shared filter propagates this into ranking, selection, and branch choices.

- **P2 — Both architectures are not always preserved.** For `stateless or stateful_service workload port`, the architecture filter retains both, but [terraform-property-selection.ts:61](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-selection.ts:61) extracts `stateful_service` as a mandatory schema identifier. Canonical `service.port` is discarded before the conflict check, allowing a stateful leaf selection. The added tests cover `stateful or stateless`, missing this identifier spelling.

- **P2 — The new conflict behavior leaks into other providers.** [terraform-property-selection.ts:244](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-selection.ts:244) lacks a `provider_name === "workload"` guard. For another provider with equivalent `service.port` and `stateful_service.port` candidates, `stateless or stateful service.port` now forces architecture choices despite the explicit path. This exceeds the workload-only scope.

The canonical mapping agrees with the checked-in prose: `service` has no per-replica state; `stateful_service` maintains it. Existing provider/node filters remain intact in the reviewed call path.

**I would hold source approval for these findings.** No edits, agents, GitHub changes, benchmark authoring, or qualification runs were performed. The reported 276 passes and pinned resolver result remain supplied evidence, not independently verified here.
